title: tc-ai-side-pane
description:
An assistant docked beside a page: a conversation about what's on it, with history, starters, a reflection gate for
high-stakes answers and the full chat composer. Resizable, collapses to a rail, a sheet on narrow screens.

heading.description: The pane's title, its landmark's and dialog's name

messages.description: The conversation, oldest first. The app owns it

reflectionSkippable.description: Lets people skip the reflection gate

starters.description: Suggestions before the first message – derive them from what's on the page

startersTitle.description: The heading over the suggestions – unset reads "From <page>" or "Suggestions"

conversations.description: Past conversations for the History panel – unset hides History

pageContext.description: What's on the page – the composer's page-context chip; unset shows no chip

disclaimer.description: The line under the composer; "" hides it

models.description: The models in the toolbar's menu – the composer's defaults when unset

model.description: The picked model's id – the first model when empty

settings.description: The model settings in the toolbar's settings popover

settingsModel.description: Which settings the model supports – the settings button shows only with it

prompts.description: Templates for the toolbar's prompt library – the prompts button shows only with them

selectProject.description: Shows "Select a project" in the composer's menu (it fires tc-select-project)

demo.description: The composer's demo mode: dictation and approval are simulated

defaultWidth.description: The width Enter and a double-click on the edge go back to, in px

minWidth.description: The narrowest the pane can be dragged, in px

maxWidth.description: The widest the pane can be dragged, in px

shortcut.description: Opens the pane (or moves focus into it; pressed inside, closes it). "mod" is ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; "" turns it off

breakpoint.description: Below this width of the element, in px, the pane is an overlay sheet instead of docked

launcher.description: A floating "Ask AI" button while the pane is closed – false if your page has its own

text.description: What the person wrote, or the answer – may grow while `streaming` is set

context.description: User messages: what was attached from the page, shown under the message, e.g. "Q3 report"

sources.description: Assistant: the sources the answer cites ([1] in the text is the first) – shown with ai-answer

claims.description: Assistant: the answer as claims – when given, it's shown with claim-answer instead of ai-answer

claimSources.description: Assistant: the passages the claims rest on

counter.description: Assistant (claims): the strongest case against the answer

followUps.description: Assistant: follow-up questions offered under the finished answer

streaming.description: Assistant: more text is still coming

reflect.description: Assistant: a high-stakes answer – the reflection gate asks for this pause before it's relied on. "prior" hides the answer until the person has said what they expect

error.description: Assistant: the answer failed – shown as an alert with Try again

title.description: Headline of the page, message or document

name.description: Short name shown on the citation chip, e.g. "Notion"

snippet.description: The passage the answer relies on – shown in the preview

text.description: The claim's words. Spaces at the start or end are kept outside the mark

source.description: Where it came from; leave it out for connecting text that claims nothing

confidence.description: How sure the model is, 0–1 – shown no higher than the type's ceiling and the `recognition`

recognition.description: Media types: how well the medium was read, 0–1 – OCR or speech-recognition confidence, shown beside the type ("OCR 87%"); the claim's confidence is shown no higher

uncertainty.description: Why it can't be certain, when that applies

note.description: A sentence on the uncertainty or the inference, e.g. "Only two studies, both small"

sources.description: Ids of the sources it rests on

AnswerClaim.description: One claim of the answer – or, without `source`, plain text between claims

ClaimSourceType.description: Where a claim came from: a retrieved source, the model's own knowledge, an inference from other claims – or a medium, or memory

ClaimMediaType.description: Read from a medium rather than a text: a machine transcript, a video, a recording, an image, or text read off a scan (OCR)

ClaimMemoryType.description: Remembered rather than retrieved now: an earlier session, the team's shared knowledge, or another agent's finding

ClaimUncertainty.description: Why a claim can't be certain: the world hasn't decided · the evidence is thin · it's beyond what the model can know

title.description: Headline of the page or document

quote.description: The passage the claim relies on

validity.description: How fresh the source is – shown as a tc-validity-badge

ClaimSource.description: A passage a claim rests on

observed.description: When the evidence was observed or published

band.description: The band, set outright – `observed` and the profile are then ignored

changed.description: The source has changed since it was used – the app compares what was relied on with what is there now

label.description: Strip: what the paragraph is called in its tooltip and to screen readers (default "Paragraph 2")

ValidityInfo.description: What a piece of evidence says about its freshness – one paragraph of a strip, or a source in tc-claim-answer

ValidityTime.description: A moment: epoch ms, an ISO date string or a Date

ValidityProfileName.description: Built-in decay profiles – fast: hours and days (prices, status, news) · standard: weeks and months · slow: years (reference material) · lasting: never decays

ValidityProfile.description: The band boundaries, as an age in days: younger than `high` is high, than `good` good, than `aging` aging; older is stale

text.description: What's sent, or put in the composer

label.description: What the row shows, when shorter than the text – defaults to the text

hint.description: A lighter line after the label, e.g. where the suggestion comes from: “From your last report”

icon.description: A built-in icon's name or an Element (cloned) – defaults to the group's

mode.description: Overrides the list's `mode` for this suggestion – "fill" for prompts with a blank to complete

PromptStarterMode.description: What choosing a suggestion does: send it as it is, or put it in the composer to edit first

updatedAt.description: Last activity: epoch ms, an ISO string or a Date

folder.description: The id of the folder it's in

summary.description: The session's structured summary – findings, open questions, next steps – which can be loaded as context

kind.description: What kind of item, e.g. "Finding", "Open question", "Next step"

ChatSummaryItem.description: One part of a session's structured summary

tokens.description: Tokens this item takes in the window

kind.description: "file", "mention", "source" – or your own (it picks the icon and the meter colour)

pinned.description: Kept in context when the conversation is compacted

hint.description: Shown as the chip's tooltip, e.g. a path or a URL

speed.description: In the toolbar's model menu: strengths from 1 to 5 (cost 5 is the most expensive)

latencyMs.description: In the toolbar's model menu: typical time to the first token, in milliseconds

pricePerM.description: In the toolbar's model menu: price per million output tokens, in dollars

ModelParamValue.description: A value a parameter can take

category.description: Small tag next to the title, e.g. "Sales"

tone.description: Color of the tag – by default each category gets its own color in the order they appear

body.description: The prompt with variables in curly braces, e.g. "Summarize this for {audience}"

description.description: What to put in – shown on the tray while the field is focused or hovered
